label: nyiso 51 floor rederive
definition: (PROBE — NOT a keeper swap) NYISO CT/ST reliability-floor re-derivation (rule 17/18/23), floors-alone config; one-delta vs nyiso-48 head-regate, all years 2023-2025. Two source-grounded narrowings: (1) the NYC CT_PEAKER 24h hot step (tmax 31.7 / 0.1833) DISABLED (r1_disabled) — the D-4 off-window binder that double-floored NYC CT on top of the windowed NYC_CT_ev ramp and bound all 24h incl. overnight where measured CAMPD NYC CT CF~=0.018 (rule 17/18); (2) the Long Island local self-supply floor NARROWED to the HB14-21 peak window (its LCR/cable-import driver binds only at the summer design-cooling peak, not overnight) — the 0.45 fraction (residual-identified, issue #1345) is UNCHANGED, only the hours it binds. RESULT: C7 diurnal (D-1) FAIL->PASS all years (2024 CT_PEAKER off-peak cv_ratio 0.454 -> 2.393). CT_PEAKER 4.46/4.51/4.73 -> 3.70/2.84/3.86 TWh (actual 2.26/2.13/2.84), C1 CT_PEAKER FAIL->in band; free-class stays 9/10 (remaining fail = 2024 ST_GAS -3.48, the pre-existing steam under-run). self-supply CT forcing HALVED (1.84/2.87/1.86 -> 0.90/1.23/0.89 TWh); reliability-floor CT overnight energy = 0.000 (was ~0.18 from the NYC step). NOT a keeper: rule-20 D-2 CT_PEAKER forced-share still >10% (reliability alone 25.6/34.1/25.1%) and C3a -16.2/-15.5/-13.6% / C3c 0/0/7h still FAIL — both now cleanly the missing #1344 peaker-scarcity/reserve price structure (CT peakers stay economically idle without it, so the floors carry the CT commitment). D-4 residual (~35%) is entirely hour 14 (0 overnight) — a boundary artifact between D-4's hardcoded canonical CT window h15-21 and the source-derived NYISO ramp HB14-21. Rules 1/17/18/23; #1344 out of scope (parallel LP-core refactor).
